title_en: Several Opinions of the Supreme People's Court on Further Strengthening the Work of People's Tribunals under the New Situation
full_text_en:
Supreme People's Court

Several Opinions on Further Strengthening the Work of People's Tribunals under the New Situation

Fa Fa [2014] No. 21

To thoroughly implement the guiding principles of the 18th National Congress of the Communist Party of China, the Third and Fourth Plenary Sessions of the 18th Central Committee, the "Decision of the Central Committee of the Communist Party of China on Major Issues Concerning Comprehensively Deepening Reforms," and the "Decision of the Central Committee of the Communist Party of China on Major Issues Concerning Comprehensively Advancing the Rule of Law," to effectively give full play to the functions of people's tribunals, and to promote the continuous scientific development of people's tribunal work, the following opinions are hereby put forward on further strengthening the work of people's tribunals under the new situation.

I. Develop a Profound Understanding of the New Situation and New Tasks, and Accurately Grasp the Functional Positioning of People's Tribunals

1. Correctly understand the new situation. The tasks of implementing the requirements of comprehensively deepening reforms, promoting the construction of a Safe China and a Rule of Law China, deepening the reform of the judicial system, meeting the diversified judicial needs of the people, and advancing the modernization of the national governance system and governance capacity constitute the new situation facing the people's courts in the current and future period. As the "grassroots of the grassroots" of the people's courts, people's tribunals are a crucial link in deepening judicial system reform and comprehensively advancing the rule of law. They will inevitably face more severe tests, encounter more complex issues, and undertake more arduous tasks.

2. Develop a profound understanding of the new tasks. People's tribunals shall continue to give full play to their adjudicative functions, actively participate in grassroots social governance, innovate and implement measures to benefit and facilitate the people, conduct circuit trials in accordance with local conditions, combine the independent exercise of adjudicative power with the expansion of judicial democracy, strive to build a "window" for transparent justice, enhance social recognition of people's justice, and promote socialist core values. People's courts at all levels shall effectively optimize the layout of people's tribunals, actively yet prudently advance judicial reform in people's tribunals, improve the management and guarantee mechanisms for people's tribunals, and strengthen the team, equipment, and information technology construction of people's tribunals. It is necessary to continuously enhance the judicial capacity of people's tribunals, so as to enable them to play an important role in achieving the overall goal of comprehensively advancing the rule of law, building a socialist rule of law system with Chinese characteristics, building a socialist country under the rule of law, and constructing a socialist rule of law order.

3. Accurately grasp the functional positioning. Firmly adhering to the main line of justice for the people and impartial justice, and independently and impartially exercising adjudicative power on behalf of the state according to law, is the core function of people's tribunals. Providing legal support for other state organs and mass autonomous organizations in mediating social disputes, providing professional guidance to People's Mediation Committees in mediating civil disputes according to law, and actively participating in grassroots social governance are important functions of people's tribunals.

II. Always Adhere to Justice for the People, and Effectively Give Play to the Adjudicative Functions of People's Tribunals

4. Optimize the regional layout. Conscientiously implement the "Decision of the Supreme People's Court on Comprehensively Strengthening the Work of People's Tribunals," adhere to the principles of "three orientations" and "two conveniences," take "clear functions, reasonable layout, fair adjudication, standardized management, capable team, and strong guarantees" as the basic requirements, and comprehensively consider the number of cases, regional area, population size, transportation conditions, and economic and social development to optimize the regional layout and personnel ratio of people's tribunals. Actively promote a tribunal layout form centered on main tribunals, supplemented by community tribunals and circuit trial points, abandon the erroneous concept of being out of touch with reality and seeking large and numerous tribunals, and avoid wasting judicial resources and difficulties in tribunal construction, management, and maintenance.

5. Standardize setup and adjustment. Basic people's courts shall, following the adjustment of urban planning and the gradual advancement of urban-rural integration development, carefully and prudently propose plans for the setup and adjustment of people's tribunals, and submit them step by step to the higher people's court for approval. Where the people have needs, the number of litigation cases is large, staffing quotas for stationed personnel exist, construction land can be secured, and construction funds are guaranteed, a people's tribunal may be added upon approval by the higher people's court. Plans for the setup and adjustment of people's tribunals that involve larger scale, a wider scope of influence, and greater need for funds and personnel shall be reported level by level to the Supreme People's Court for review and record. In areas with developed economies and a high volume of cases, exploration of setting up specialized adjudication tribunals may be conducted based on local circumstances.

6. Improve the case filing mechanism. Basic people's courts shall, based on the actual conditions of their jurisdiction, scientifically construct a mechanism for people's tribunals to directly accept case filings, and strengthen the guidance and management of case filing work in people's tribunals. For people's tribunals in economically developed areas with convenient transportation, a unified case filing method by the basic people's court may be adopted to strengthen case flow management. For people's tribunals in areas with inconvenient transportation such as mountainous areas, pastoral areas, forest regions, and remote areas, the mechanism for direct case filing by people's tribunals shall be strengthened and improved, and technical means such as remote case filing shall be used to address the difficulties parties face in filing cases. The specific scope of cases accepted by a people's tribunal shall be determined by the basic people's court to which it belongs and shall be announced to the public through certain means. For cases that should be accepted according to law, it shall be ensured that all cases that meet the filing requirements are accepted, and all lawsuits that meet the acceptance requirements are entertained. For cases that indeed should not be accepted, the reasons shall be explained to the parties.

7. Ensure a good job in adjudicating cases involving people's livelihood. In accordance with the general requirement of implementing collective ownership, stabilizing farmers' contractual rights, and invigorating land management rights, effectively protect rural land contractual relationships and farmers' land contractual management rights according to law, strengthen the real right protection for land contractual management rights, and legally protect farmers' rights to possess, use, benefit from, transfer, mortgage, and pledge their contracted land. Lawfully and properly adjudicate disputes in areas closely related to people's livelihood, and protect the legitimate rights and interests of left-behind children, left-behind women, and left-behind elderly in rural areas. Lawfully protect the ecological environment, promote the improvement of the living environment, and provide judicial guarantees for scientifically advancing the construction of a new socialist countryside.

8. Strengthen litigation services. Promote the construction of service windows in people's tribunals, and strive to provide integrated, one-stop services for litigants' litigation activities. Strengthen litigation guidance for litigants, and provide necessary procedural guidance for litigants with limited litigation capacity. For important evidence that proves difficult for the parties to collect or that is indeed necessary for the trial of the case, the court shall, upon application by the party or ex officio, take the initiative to investigate and collect evidence in a timely manner. Select and apply more economical litigation procedures and procedural measures according to law, and effectively reduce the litigation burden on the parties. Promote the improvement of the legal aid system, strengthen judicial relief efforts, and effectively ensure that the people can obtain legal assistance in a timely and effective manner.

9. Conduct circuit trials well. Correctly handle the relationship between holding court sessions in chambers and conducting circuit trials, conscientiously implement the "Opinions on Vigorously Promoting Circuit Trials to Facilitate Litigation by the People," reasonably set up circuit case-handling points and litigation service points, and improve the pertinence and effectiveness of circuit trials. In remote ethnic areas and other areas where litigation is inconvenient for the people, a work mechanism centered on circuit trials shall be established, inherit and carry forward the Ma Xiwu trial method, promote circuit trial models such as vehicle-mounted courts, and form a judicial service network that takes people's tribunals as points, vehicle-mounted mobile courts as lines, and basic people's courts as the surface, combining "points, lines, and surfaces" for full coverage. In economically developed areas with convenient transportation, the focus of circuit trials shall be on cases that have a significant impact on social harmony and stability, and that play an important role in enhancing the people's awareness of the rule of law, maintaining the socialist rule of law order, and promoting socialist moral customs.

10. Properly handle the relationship between mediation and adjudication. Give full play to the unique role of mediation in resolving grassroots civil disputes, and for civil disputes suitable for mediation, conduct mediation first according to law. Actively summarize the characteristics of different types of cases, within the framework of legal provisions, appropriately draw on village rules and civil conventions, respect good customs and social conditions and public opinion, innovate mediation work methods, and strive to completely resolve disputes from their roots. Firmly correct erroneous practices that harm the legitimate rights and interests of the parties, such as forced mediation, prolonged mediation without resolution, and the assignment of mandatory mediation or withdrawal targets, which violate the laws of adjudication. Vigorously improve the quality of adjudicative documents from people's tribunals, focus on applying the law correctly and strengthening legal reasoning, give play to the moral guidance function of judicial adjudication, highlight rules, maintain order, and promote virtue.

11. Improve enforcement work. For cases adjudicated by people's tribunals where enforcement work is relatively difficult, enforcement by the basic people's court does not affect the timely realization of the parties' legitimate rights and interests, and personnel and equipment make it difficult to guarantee the smooth progress of enforcement work, in principle, the basic people's court shall be responsible for enforcement. For cases where enforcement can be completed during the court session or where enforcement by the people's tribunal is more convenient for the litigants, the people's tribunal shall be responsible for enforcement. Where conditions permit, a direct enforcement mechanism may be explored, such as by stationing an enforcement group from the basic people's court in the tribunal, to maximize convenience for litigants and improve enforcement efficiency.

12. Improve the people's assessor system. Implement the people's assessor doubling plan, and in light of the work characteristics of people's tribunals, expand the proportion of grassroots people selected and expand the scope of cases in which they participate. Standardize the methods and procedures for determining the cases in which people's assessors participate in trial, conscientiously implement the principle of "random selection," and change the practice of having assessors permanently stationed at the tribunal. Strengthen pre-service and in-service training for people's assessors to improve their ability to perform duties. Actively explore mechanisms and methods for people's assessors to participate only in determining factual issues. Establish a mechanism for regularly adjusting funding guarantee standards, and timely and fully disburse subsidies for transportation and loss of income to people's assessors.

III. Actively Participate in Grassroots Social Governance, and Effectively Give Play to the Role of People's Tribunals as a Bridge, Link, and Judicial Guarantee

13. Provide judicial guarantees for other organizations and institutions to resolve disputes. Give full play to the role of people's tribunals as a link in the "four governance" and their exemplary and guaranteeing role in the diversified dispute resolution mechanism, and make positive contributions to improving the level of rule-of-law governance in townships and counties. Proactively strengthen communication and collaboration with other grassroots state organs, mass autonomous organizations, and industry mediation organizations such as public security, judicial administration, labor dispute arbitration, rural land contract arbitration, and people's mediation committees. Respect and support their lawful mediation of social disputes, and actively work on the connection between litigation and non-litigation dispute resolution mechanisms, such as judicial confirmation.

14. Provide guidance to various types of mediation organizations. In accordance with the principle of "not absent, not overstepping, not misplaced," strengthen professional guidance to People's Mediation Committees according to law. Through the effective performance of adjudicative functions, provide a rule-of-law model and directional guidance for people's mediation, administrative mediation, and mass autonomous organizations in mediating and resolving disputes. Pay special attention to strengthening and standardizing the connection and communication with grassroots mass organizations such as residents' committees and villagers' committees in resolving disputes, and jointly maintain a good grassroots social order.

15. Participate in local governance based on adjudicative functions. People's tribunals shall flexibly use various forms such as open days for the public, observing court sessions, explaining the law through cases, and post-judgment答疑 to actively conduct legal publicity, guiding the people to consciously fulfill legal obligations, social responsibilities, and family responsibilities. They shall participate in local social governance by timely submitting special reports on litigation-related disputes to the local Party committee and People's Congress, and issuing judicial suggestions to the government and other relevant departments. They shall not exceed their adjudicative functions to participate in local administrative or economic affairs, or other affairs unrelated to their adjudicative duties, such as meetings, receiving petitions, or publicity.

IV. Actively Yet Prudently Advance the Reform of the Judicial System, and Continuously Improve the Working Mechanism of People's Tribunals

16. Carry out reform pilot projects. People's courts at all levels shall regard people's tribunals as "experimental fields" for judicial reform. In accordance with the principles of emancipating the mind, actively advancing, seeking truth from facts, and being cautious and prudent, promote reforms to be piloted first in people's tribunals. Intermediate people's courts that have people's tribunals within their jurisdiction shall select 3-5 people's tribunals to pilot reforms suitable for implementation in people's tribunals, and encourage areas with suitable conditions to actively expand the scope of pilot projects. Pilot people's tribunals shall report on the pilot work situation to their basic people's court at least once every six months, and the reports shall be summarized and reported level by level to the Supreme People's Court, to accumulate experience and create conditions for comprehensively advancing judicial system reform.

17. Implement the judicial accountability system. Follow the laws of adjudication, in accordance with the principle of unifying powers and responsibilities, explore the establishment of a responsibility system for presiding judges in handling cases, clarify the powers and responsibilities of judges in handling cases, and gradually realize that adjudicative documents are signed by the presiding judge. Where conditions permit, explore and improve the accountability system for collegiate panels handling cases, clarifying the responsibility of individual opinions and conduct in the outcome of the case. Standardize the supervisory and management authority of the chief judge of the people's tribunal over adjudicative work, ensuring that powers and responsibilities are unified, clear, and that supervision is standardized and orderly.

18. Optimize personnel composition. Establish a mechanism for quota supplementation and dynamic management to ensure that 80% of newly added quotas are used for the grassroots and the front line of adjudication, and timely replenish personnel according to work needs. Adhere to an endogenous path of team development. Explore the formation of trial teams centered on presiding judges based on the volume of adjudication work, equipping them with the necessary number of judicial assistants, clerks, and other adjudicative support personnel. Strengthen adjudicative support forces through methods such as purchasing services, to solve the problem of "one-person tribunals" or "two-person tribunals" arising from insufficient adjudicative personnel in some places. Improve the classified management system for judicial personnel, stabilize the adjudication team, and improve the quality and efficiency of adjudication.

19. Improve professional guarantees. Advance the reform of the professional rank sequence and salary system for judges, gradually improve the rank and treatment of grassroots judges, achieve appropriately higher positions, ranks, and judge grades for judges in people's tribunals, and moderately tilt salary and welfare policies towards grassroots courts and people's tribunals. People's tribunals may first pilot salary determination methods such as salary plus case-handling subsidies and post allowances. Strengthen occupational risk guarantees, and improve relief and compensation systems for death in the line of duty, accidental injury, etc. When exploring and promoting the unified management of personnel, funds, and property of local courts below the provincial level, as well as reforms such as delayed retirement and rehiring of judges, higher people's courts shall pay attention to considering the characteristics and needs of people's tribunals.

20. Improve adjudication management. Eliminate management and assessment indicators that do not conform to the laws of adjudication, are not conducive to the work of people's tribunals, and are prone to cause erroneous guidance. Clarify the classification standards for summary cases and complex/difficult cases, reasonably allocate adjudicative resources, and achieve the separation of simple and complex cases. Explore the use of simplified documents such as forms, writs, and element-based formats in small claims litigation and other suitable summary cases to expedite the trial process. Explore a working system for the centralized and specialized handling of adjudicative support matters, allowing judges to focus on adjudication.

21. Strengthen judicial transparency. Fully disclose information on tribunal personnel, management systems, codes of conduct, and litigation guides. Timely disclose case information, judicial bases, litigation procedures, and adjudicative results according to law, to satisfy the parties' right to know and eliminate black-box operations. When promoting the construction of the "three platforms," pay attention to considering the work characteristics of people's tribunals. Actively leverage the unique advantages of people's tribunals being rooted in the grassroots. On the premise of ensuring judicial safety, simplify procedures for attending court sessions to meet the public's demand for attendance; carry out thematic activities on judicial openness, proactively invite and organize representatives from all sectors of society to observe court sessions and visit tribunal work; further leverage the unique role of circuit trials in judicial openness and legal publicity, and enhance social recognition of tribunal work.

V. Effectively Strengthen Team Building and Organizational Leadership, and Continuously Improve the Team Quality and Material Equipment Guarantee Level of People's Tribunals

22. Strengthen Party building work. Adhere to the principle of "building Party branches in tribunals," achieving full coverage of Party organizations and Party work. A people's tribunal with three or more Party members shall establish a Party branch; a people's tribunal with fewer than three Party members may establish a joint Party branch. The organizational relationship of the Party branch of the people's tribunal shall be subordinate to the basic people's court to which it belongs. Strengthen the organizational functions of the Party branch in the people's tribunal, strictly enforce inner-Party life, and give full play to the branch's functions of educating, managing, and supervising officers. Focus on using information networks and new media to carry out Party building work.

23. Select good chief judges of tribunals. Actively implement the institutional level of people's tribunals and the rank of the chief judge of the people's tribunal. Give priority to selecting judges at the section level or above who have experience working in tribunals to serve as chief judges of people's tribunals. For people's tribunals in municipalities directly under the central government and tribunals with a large number of cases and heavy tasks, judges at the division level may be selected. Deputy chief judges may be set up in people's tribunals as needed. Give priority to selecting leaders of basic people's courts from among those who have experience serving as chief judges of people's tribunals.

24. Improve the system of regular job rotation and temporary training assignments. Promote orderly personnel exchanges between people's tribunals, and between people's tribunals and other divisions of the basic people's court. A chief judge of a people's tribunal shall generally rotate positions once every three to five years after taking office. Newly recruited personnel by basic people's courts shall generally be first assigned to a people's tribunal for training and exercise for a period of not less than one year. When basic people's courts select judges to go to higher people's courts or courts in developed regions for study and training, judges from people's tribunals shall be given priority. When higher people's courts select and transfer judges, they shall accept a certain proportion of judges with work experience in people's tribunals. When higher people's courts select cadres with promising futures to go to the grassroots level, they shall give priority to arranging for them to take temporary training assignments in people's tribunals.

25. Implement the responsibility for Party conduct and integrity construction. The Party leading group of the basic people's court shall include the Party conduct and integrity construction of people's tribunals within the scope of its main responsibility. For major disciplinary or illegal cases occurring in a people's tribunal, in addition to holding the directly responsible persons accountable, relevant leading cadres of the court shall be held accountable in accordance with the provisions on the responsibility system for Party conduct and integrity construction. The discipline inspection and supervision department of the basic people's court shall earnestly perform its supervision duties. Through judicial affairs inspections and special inspections, timely detect and correct problems in the discipline and work style of officers in people's tribunals, and seriously investigate and handle disciplinary and illegal cases with a "zero tolerance" attitude. The chief judge of the people's tribunal shall conscientiously fulfill the "dual responsibilities" of his/her position, managing and leading the team well while performing adjudicative work, ensuring that the people's tribunal is impartial and honest in its justice.

26. Strengthen discipline and work style construction. Continuously strengthen education on ideals and beliefs, guide officers in people's tribunals to firmly establish the mass viewpoint, enhance feelings for the masses, and effectively solve the "six difficulties and three types of problematic cases" strongly reflected by the masses. Adhere to strict education, strict management, and strict supervision, and resolutely rectify unhealthy practices in the work of people's tribunals. Relying on information technology, comprehensively build a risk prevention and control mechanism for clean government that meets the work characteristics of people's tribunals, effectively strengthen supervision and restriction over the operation of adjudicative power in people's tribunals, and enhance the execution of judicial integrity systems. Place work style construction in a prominent position, integrate it into daily work, and use systems to ensure the standardization, normalization, and long-term effectiveness of improving judicial work style.

27. Improve tribunal management. Improve tribunal management rules and regulations, focus on routine management, and pay attention to improving the assessment and evaluation mechanism by soliciting opinions from the grassroots masses. Focus on identifying and publicizing advanced models of people's tribunals, and timely commend and reward outstanding officers in people's tribunals. Strengthen the construction of cultural and sports venues, implement the system of vacations and recuperation, organize regular physical examinations, strengthen humanistic care and psychological counseling for officers, and help solve practical difficulties in work, study, and life.

28. Improve education and training. Regularly conduct rotational training for chief judges of people's tribunals, ensuring that judges of people's tribunals receive no less than 7 days of professional training each year. Adhere to hierarchical and categorized training, give full play to the leading role of judge training institutions at all levels, actively utilize the training resources of other training institutions and higher education institutions, and promote the extension and tilt of high-quality education and training resources toward people's tribunals through various means. Adhere to a demand-oriented direction for training that closely follows adjudicative practice. Further increase support for training in the western and ethnic regions, and strengthen the training of bilingual judges.

29. Strengthen infrastructure construction. High people's courts shall, in accordance with the requirements of the Twelfth Five-Year Plan for infrastructure construction of people's courts, rationally arrange annual construction plans and strive to fully complete the existing infrastructure construction tasks of people's tribunals during the Twelfth Five-Year Plan period. New people's tribunals shall, based on the Construction Standards for Courtrooms of People's Courts, reasonably determine the construction scale according to factors such as the authorized strength of the tribunal and the number of cases accepted annually, strictly review the design plan, and install unified signage in accordance with the requirements of the Norms for Unified Signage Setup of People's Tribunals.

30. Enhance the ability to guarantee funding. Grassroots people's courts shall, based on the work tasks of people's tribunals and the needs for equipment allocation and information technology construction, properly prepare budgets for people's tribunals and disburse funds in a timely manner. High people's courts shall strengthen guidance and supervision over the use and management of funds for people's tribunals. They shall, in a planned and step-by-step manner, equip people's tribunals with necessary case-handling and office equipment, raise the level of equipment allocation year by year, and improve trial work conditions. By 2015, the equipment allocation of all people's tribunals nationwide shall reach the level required by the Guiding Standards for Basic Business Equipment Allocation of Grassroots People's Courts.

31. Promote information technology construction. High people's courts shall take the "Balance Project" construction as a starting point, focus on the management of people's tribunals and convenience for the people, reasonably determine the content and scale of information technology construction for people's tribunals, and increase investment and funding guarantees. In accordance with the requirements of the Supreme People's Court's Decision on Comprehensively Strengthening the Informatization Work of People's Courts and the Five-Year Plan for Informatization Construction of People's Courts, people's tribunals in the eastern region shall be connected to the information network system of grassroots people's courts by the end of 2014, in the central region by the end of 2015, and in the western region by the end of 2016. It is necessary to ensure that the software and hardware configuration of the people's court information system meets the needs of litigation service work of people's tribunals, equip people's tribunals with necessary informatized office and case-handling equipment and software, optimize work procedures, and improve work efficiency and user-friendliness.

32. Emphasize safety management. It is necessary to establish and improve the supervision mechanism, enhance safety prevention awareness, overcome lax and paralytic thinking and luck mentality, and solidly carry out daily security protection work. In accordance with the requirements of "necessary, sufficient, and timely," in principle, each people's tribunal shall be equipped with at least one judicial police officer, and with a number of security personnel as needed. Improve the allocation of various safety prevention facilities and equipment such as security checks, explosion-proof, monitoring, and liquid hazardous substance detection, give priority to improving the safety and danger prevention hardware conditions of people's tribunals, ensure that "human prevention, physical prevention, and technical prevention" in people's tribunals are implemented in place, and strictly prevent all types of major and serious safety liability accidents.

33. Promote theoretical research. People's courts at all levels shall, based on their different functional positions, create conditions for flourishing theoretical research on people's tribunals, strengthen various forms of exchange and cooperation with legal education and research institutions, pool forces from multiple sources, explore the establishment of a working mechanism for theoretical research on people's tribunals, and conduct in-depth theoretical research work on people's tribunals. Focus on studying the status and role of people's tribunals in the socialist judicial system with Chinese characteristics under the new situation, the functional positioning of people's tribunals and their role in social governance, and how people's tribunals can carry out work of justice for the people, convenience for the people, and benefit for the people in the process of advancing judicial reform, and other comprehensive and forward-looking major topics. Taking problems as the orientation, summarize and refine materials and topics for theoretical research from the judicial practice of people's tribunals, form theoretical research results, effectively achieve the transformation of results, and guide and promote the scientific development of the work of people's tribunals.

34. Strengthen supervision and guidance. The Party groups of people's courts at all levels shall effectively assume the leadership responsibility for the work of people's tribunals. People's courts at the intermediate level and above shall establish specialized offices for guiding the work of people's tribunals, adhere to the principle of classified guidance, and enhance the pertinence and effectiveness of guidance. Supervising and guiding the work of people's tribunals shall be taken as an important part of the daily work of people's courts at all levels, improve the mechanisms for problem discovery, feedback, analysis, and resolution, and establish mechanisms for risk assessment, early warning, and mitigation of major sensitive cases.

December 4, 2014
